core_obligations: Reduce to injectivity by the bijective-map statement (proof line 5488)
Assume two distinct points with the same image: choose disjoint open neighbourhoods and note that the images of their complements are closed and cover the target (proof lines 5489-5495)

Contradiction: the technical containment puts the common image in the closures of both complements, while closures of disjoint opens in an extremally disconnected space are disjoint (proof lines 5496-5499)
proof_roadmap: 由「紧 Hausdorff 间双射是同胚」，只需证单射。
设 f(x) = f(x') = y 而 x ≠ x'，取不交开邻域 U, U'；f 闭 ⇒ T = f(X∖U)、T' = f(X∖U') 闭，且 Y = T ∪ T'。
由 image-open-technical 得 y ∈ 闭包(Y∖T) ∩ 闭包(Y∖T')；而 extremally disconnected 中不交开集的闭包不交（intersection-empty），矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a surjective continuous map of quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces onto an extremally disconnected space which never maps a proper closed subset onto the target is a homeomorphism (author lemma at source lines 5480-5486, label lemma-isomorphism). The proof (source lines 5488-5500) reduces to injectivity, assumes two distinct points with the same image, separates them by disjoint open neighbourhoods, uses closedness of the map and the technical containment to place the image in two disjoint closures, contradicting the extremal disconnectedness (proof lines 5488-5499). The closure contradiction is the substance. H3.
